_meta.title: Visitor mode (brief 1, 9.1, 9.5): access rules, guard posts, the stop, the halmi and the errand, 467 BCE
_meta.status: DATA ONLY: no runtime reads this file yet. The lead implements visitor mode from it. Every Terrace rule, post kind, wait and step is reconstruction (C) unless its row says otherwise; no text describes anyone being stopped at Persepolis.
_meta.frame: grid metres (x = grid east, y = grid north), as site_spec.json, footprints.json, people_places.json, settlement.json, town.json and town_plots.json. NO NEW GEOMETRY: every `at` is copied from the file and field named in `at_from`; zones are named by existing ids (ref = file: id); three derived zones (terrace_courts, treasury_street, pf_archive_findspot) are defined only by reference to existing geometry.
_meta.tiers: A attested / B inferred (search extracts capped at B; Greek and biblical claims about other palaces at most B) / C reconstructed
weak: No text describes a guard check at Persepolis: every Terrace post kind and the stop procedure are C, built from B practice elsewhere (HDT, XEN-CYR, Ezra).
Guards in the tablets are not confirmed (PEOPLE §4 GAP); PF lance-bearers were labour inspectors and escorts (HENK2002, SX).
The halmi evidence is Darius-era (509-493) plus the later Arshama authorisation; nobody is known to have issued halmis in 467 (Q-120).
All waits and processing times are C (Q-125).
The town has no rendered road station; stables-0001 is proposed as the post station and the visitor's lodging (D-104, C).
Arshama's no-rations-for-extra-days clause conflicts with the simulation's 1-5 day station stays (Q-128).

rule_levels.open: walk in freely; people may look; nobody asks
rule_levels.business: only with the halmi shown and a stated business that belongs to this place (the errand step that is current names it); otherwise turned back
rule_levels.escort: only with a guard or official walking beside the visitor (given at a check post when the business lies beyond); alone he is turned back
rule_levels.closed: no entry in visitor mode and no escort offered, except where an errand step names an explicit exception
rule_levels.observer_mode: nothing is barred (brief 1); these rules apply only with PLAYER_MODE = visitor

terrace_open.note: aligned with lives.json work_day (sunrise+0.4 to sunset-0.6); outside these hours the Terrace is closed to the visitor (XEN-CYR 4.5.14 sentinels refuse admission before daylight; 7.5.25-27 palace gates locked at night with a guard before them: B claims, Babylon/camp)

content.item: officials along the route by name; provisions given by each in turn, stage by stage
content.note: A for the Arshama document, B as a model

content.item: no rations for extra days: 'If he should be more than one day in a place, then for these days do not give them any rations'
the bearer's business; validity; return journey

form.v: leather, folded and tied, sealed with a clay bulla whose seal image suppliers had learned to recognise
form.note: the Elamite Q texts record the halmi and are not it; whether any halmi was clay is unknown (Q-122)

carried_and_shown.v: carried by the traveller ('he carried a sealed document of X'); shown to the supplier at each ration point; the receipt tablet sealed by supplier and recipient went to Persepolis for accounting

entitles.v: travel rations at road stations a day apart: 1-1.5 qa flour and about 1 qa wine or beer per person per day
a guide (barrisdama) for select individuals and large groups
as a 'letter order': an issue of goods from a store to a named receiver (PF 15)
NOT attested: that a halmi opened any door on the Terrace

checks_attested.v: the supplier's check at the ration point (the Q-text formula records whose halmi it was)

checks_not_attested.v: any check at the Gate, the stairs, the Treasury door or the town: C, by analogy with palace gates and road guards elsewhere (HDT 1.123, 3.72, 3.77, 3.118, 3.140, 5.35, 5.52, 7.239; XEN-CYR 4.5.14, 7.5.25-27; Ezra 5:9-10)

identity.v: a messenger (Elam. hutlak, PF 45) of an unnamed official, travelling alone on foot, no guide

halmi.issuer: the satrap at Susa (office only; the 467 holder is unknown)
halmi.route: Susa -> Parsa (the royal road, 23 stages, ~552 km per one summary)
halmi.form: folded leather, tied, clay bulla; never opened in the world; no text rendered (brief 10: published texts only)
halmi.note: D-101; B pattern (issuer at the point of departure), C instance

letter.v: a sealed letter for the treasurer at Parsa (content unknown to the visitor and never shown): Aramaic on leather with a bulla
letter.note: PT letters are orders from officials addressed to the treasurer (B); the medium follows the inter-provincial letters (B); the instance is C

PF lance-bearers served primarily as labour inspectors and escorts of groups, not as military personnel
guards in Persian and Median dress on the stair facades (Apadana, Tachara XPc, Hadish XPd, Tripylon): a motif, not a list of posts
the palace guard of spearmen stands 'about the palace day and night, whenever he was in residence; but whenever he went away anywhere, they went along'
guards_evidence.note: claim (Cyropaedia 7.5.68); supports the smaller garrison with the king absent (D-003)

guards_evidence.v: the Terrace garrison of the build: 100 men in 10 files, three watches (D-023)
the 'garrison quarters' near the SE corner: 'quarters for members of the garrison and perhaps for artisans' vs 'function unknown ... name conventional'

stop_procedure.act: a guard is always at the post

at 8-15 m the nearer guard turns to face the visitor

stop_procedure.act: step into the way; open hand raised; spear upright, butt to the ground, never levelled
stop_procedure.basis: relief guards stand with the spear upright (B stance); the rest C
stop_procedure.build: half a pace into the way

stop_procedure.basis: court messengers 'asked the seven why they had come' (HDT 3.77.2); 'Who commanded you ...? We asked their names also' (Ezra 5:9-10)

stop_procedure.act: look at the bulla, not read the leather
stop_procedure.basis: the bulla's seal image 'suppliers and other officials ... had learned to recognise' (HALMI-SX, B); a royal letter is read by a scribe (HDT 3.128.3, B)

stop_procedure.build: the visitor shows the letter's bulla; optional composed line arc:ʾgrh + arc:gdbr ('letter ... treasurer')

stop_procedure.act: word goes in; the stranger waits
stop_procedure.basis: Syloson 'sat in the king's antechamber ... the doorkeeper brought word ... [and] brought Syloson in' (HDT 3.140.1-3)
stop_procedure.build: Gate: the visitor sits on the bench in gate_hall while one guard fetches an escort (patrol pair or an off-watch man, D-023), 0.2-0.7 h. Treasury: the letter is carried in, the visitor waits in treasury_street

stop_procedure.basis: 'the gatekeeper and the messenger forbade him' (HDT 3.118.2)
stop_procedure.build: a flat hand and a gesture back toward the stair or out of the street; no words beyond the lexicon; no threat

the two men of the post close the way with their bodies; the patrol pair comes; they walk him to the zone edge (the stair head; the Gate for the courts). NO blows, NO weapons, NO arrest, NO punishment shown (brief 9.1 no combat; 12 not sensational)

stop_procedure.basis: the guards at Susa knew the leading Persians by sight (HDT 3.77.1, B)
stop_procedure.build: log a 'stopped' encounter (lives.json familiarity 0.5, half-life 6 days); outcome admitted / turned_back feeds the recognition rules

errand.title: A sealed letter for the treasurer at Parsa
errand.why: the Treasury archive is the one archive live in 467 (dated PT texts peak in Xerxes yrs 19-20, B); its letters are orders from officials addressed to the treasurer (B); messengers carry officials' orders (PF 45, A Darius-era); halmis for journeys from Parsa are issued by the Parsa administration (B); rations against the sealed document (B). Each link B; the chain C

timing.answer: letter handed in before midday -> answer the next morning from sunrise + 1 h; after midday -> the morning after next
timing.silver_day: +1 day if E-05 (silver weighed out) runs at the Treasury that day
timing.note: no evidence for any processing time (Q-125); these rules only make the waiting visible and the next day different

steps.action: show the halmi; draw the day's ration; the keeper's scribe writes a receipt that the keeper and the visitor seal
steps.receive: the day's ration (1.5 qa flour, 1 qa wine or beer)
steps.note: B practice, C place (the first station out of Persepolis is unidentified)

steps.action: on arrival in the town: show the halmi, draw the day's ration; a receipt is sealed
the climb (open); the stair-head guards watch
the stop (stop_procedure): 'halmi?'; the bulla; the letter's bulla and 'ʾgrh ... gdbr'; a guard goes for an escort; the visitor waits on the bench
walk with the escort; doors of closed zones are passed, not entered

hand over the letter; a Treasury man takes it to the scribes (treasury_desk); E-81 doubles the door; the visitor waits in the street until word comes back ('tomorrow', by gesture and arc:ywm + arc:ḥd); the escort walks him back to the Gate
steps.note: PT letters are addressed to the treasurer and kept in the Treasury (B). Variant B: escorted to treasury_desk for the hand-over (treasury_desk errand_exception)

steps.action: the night in town; his keep while he waits on business is issued by the storekeeper against the halmi (C; Arshama gives no rations for extra days: Q-128)
steps.note: D-104: stables-0001 as post station and lodging (C)

steps.action: next morning: recognised at the Gate (recognition rules), he goes on alone (or escorted if not recognised); at the door he receives the Treasury's sealed answer to the sender
steps.receive: a sealed answer (clay tablet sealed on its squared left edge, the PT form, B; or leather with a bulla)

steps.action: ask for a halmi for the return journey (journeys from Parsa carry a halmi of the Parsa administration: B pattern); show the Susa halmi and the Treasury's answer; the doorkeeper takes them in; wait
who: the official (the office of Parnakka's successor; unnamed in 467)
steps.wait_h: same day if before midday, otherwise next morning
steps.receive: a new halmi (folded leather, bulla) for the road out of Parsa

steps.action: draw the first day's ration for the road
leave by the royal road W; the errand closes
